'''David Warren McLaughlin''' (born October 11, 1944) is an applied mathematician and academic administrator whose work concerns [[nonlinear systems]], nonlinear waves, and mathematical models of [[visual neuroscience]]. McLaughlin served as the provost of [[New York University]] from 2002 to 2016.

==Early life and education==

McLaughlin grew up in [[Woodbine, Iowa]], where his father sold gas to farmers.<ref name="Nuzzo2006">{{cite journal |last=Nuzzo |first=Regina |title=Profile of David W. McLaughlin |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |year=2006 |volume=103 |issue=20 |pages=7539–7541 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0602260103 |doi-access=free |pmid=16682627 |pmc=1472482 }}</ref> 
He attended [[Creighton University]] in [[Omaha, Nebraska]], majoring in physics and mathematics and graduating [[summa cum laude]] in 1966.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /> McLaughlin went on to graduate study at [[Indiana University (Bloomington)]] where he studied [[theoretical physics]] with [[Lawrence Schulman|Larry Schulman]], completing a Ph.D. in physics in 1971.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" />

==Career==

McLaughlin moved several times within a few years at the beginning of his career. He first joined New York University in 1971 as an assistant professor in mathematics, recruited by [[Joseph Keller]], but had to leave in 1972 when NYU's University Heights campus in the Bronx was sold due to financial problems.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /> He next moved to [[Iowa State University]] in 1972, again as an assistant professor of mathematics, and then joined the [[University of Arizona]] as associate professor in 1974. <ref name="Nuzzo2006" /> He served on the faculty at the University of Arizona for 15 years, during which time he was the chair of the applied mathematics program.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" />

In 1989, McLaughlin joined [[Princeton University]] as professor of mathematics, where he directed the applied and computational mathematics program before returning to NYU in 1994 as director of the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]].<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /> At Courant, he led efforts in mathematics, applied mathematics, computational science, and computer science, recruiting faculty in these areas and developing programs in atmosphere-ocean studies, financial mathematics, multimedia technology, and computational biology.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /> He was appointed the provost of NYU in 2002, serving in that role for 14 years.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" />. He is currently the Silver Professor of Mathematics and Neural Science at the Courant Institute.<ref name="NYUProvostEmeritus" />

==Research==
McLaughlin's work was applied mathematics focused on large-scale nonlinear systems best described by [[partial differential equations]], with a long interest in mathematical models of complex systems.<ref name="NASMcLaughlin" /> His research areas included nonlinear waves, laser beams, and in recent years, neuronal networks for visual neural science. <ref name="NASMcLaughlin" /> His early research used [[Asymptotic analysis|asymptotic methods]] applied to [[Path integral formulation|path integrals]] and the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]].<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /><ref name="McLaughlin1986">{{cite journal |last1=McLaughlin |first1=D. W. |last2=Papanicolaou |first2=G. C. |last3=Sulem |first3=C. |last4=Sulem |first4=P. L. |title=Focusing singularity of the cubic Schrödinger equation |journal=Physical Review A |year=1986 |volume=34 |issue=2 |pages=1200–1210 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.34.1200 |pmid=9897379 }}</ref> His major work was on nonlinear dispersive waves, including systems where wave dissipation is weak, and his work addressed coherent behavior, chaotic behavior, and dispersive wave turbulence.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /><ref name="Majda1997">{{cite journal |last1=Majda |first1=A. J. |last2=McLaughlin |first2=D. W. |last3=Tabak |first3=E. G. |title=A one-dimensional model for dispersive wave turbulence |journal=Journal of Nonlinear Science |year=1997 |volume=7 |pages=9–44 |doi=10.1007/BF02679124}}</ref>

After returning to the Courant, he developed an interest in neuroscience; he collaborated with [[Robert Shapley]] at NYU’s Center for Neural Science, working at the intersection of mathematics and neuroscience.<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /><ref name="Tao2006">{{cite journal |last1=Tao |first1=Louis |last2=Cai |first2=David |last3=McLaughlin |first3=David W. |last4=Shelley |first4=Michael J. |last5=Shapley |first5=Robert |title=Orientation selectivity in visual cortex by fluctuation-controlled criticality |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |year=2006 |volume=103 |issue=34 |pages=12911–12916 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0605415103 |doi-access=free |pmid=16905648 |pmc=1562545}}</ref> With a focus on visual neuroscience, McLaughlin developed large-scale computational models of the front end of the cortical visual system, particularly the [[primary visual cortex]].<ref name="NASMcLaughlin" />

==Honors and awards==
* Member, [[National Academy of Sciences]] (2002).<ref name="Nuzzo2006" /><ref name="NASMcLaughlin">{{cite web |title=David W. McLaughlin |website=National Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/david-w-mclaughlin-wycakl/ |access-date=2026-05-15}}</ref>
* Fellow, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2000).<ref name="AmAcadMcLaughlin">{{cite web |title=David W. McLaughlin |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/david-w-mclaughlin |access-date=2026-05-15}}</ref>
* Fellow, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2003). <ref name="NYUProvostEmeritus">{{cite web |title=David McLaughlin |website=New York University |url=https://www.nyu.edu/about/leadership-university-administration/provost-emeritus.html |access-date=2026-05-17}}</ref>
* Fellow, [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]<ref name="NYUProvostEmeritus" />
